rationale: Review of direct check 495d49f1 (unit-claim-install-snapshot-alignment), whose fresh execution 3d53c8e244184b0490a87411aabe15f4 completed the comparison: the declarative prerequisite longer-tail matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete are true at witness index 1, and the assertion evaluated false. A log seeded through index 5 was given a snapshot at index 3: the install was accepted, lastApplied and the snapshot index became 3, compaction left two entries above the snapshot, and the receiver's effective last entry stayed (5, term 1), so within_installed_snapshot is false. This review supplies the required checker_correspondence item and resolves the two open applicability issues that record the same snapshot-protocol conflict against the claim and against the harness legality.

review_items.rationale: Requirement versus encoded predicate: the obligation requires that after installing a snapshot at N a receiver that cannot confirm the snapshot's last included entry does not keep an unconfirmed tail; the predicate within_installed_snapshot is exactly the effective last entry being at or below N, which S54 defines through getLastEntry and S57/S58 locate as the handler's responsibility. Entry and caller duties: the harness declares the longer tail from its own seeded log (raw last index 5 above the installed index 3) and only evaluates when the install was accepted, so the comparison is not made against an unexamined premise. Identity: op_id snap-1 is on both the declaration and the result, and the prerequisite correlation matched. Oracle: the assertion is computed from emitted event fields, not from tests_passed; the run exited 0 while the predicate was false, which is the case this oracle must catch. Observation path and completion: installSnapshot is the production handler over the main-thread code path, the response was received, the substitute FSM schedule answered the restore future with success, and the run completed. Counterevidence: none of the open issues is evidence against the encoded predicate; the transient-tail reading and the adaptation limits are recorded below.
limitations: The tail was seeded directly into the caller-owned LogStore rather than produced by a real leader's replication, so reachability under a leader is a premise, not an observation.

Node goroutines were disabled and an explicit substitute answered restore futures with success; the check therefore isolates the handler's log/snapshot bookkeeping and does not exercise FSM restore, term interaction or the following AppendEntries.
conf.TrailingLogs was set to 0 so compaction was not skipped by the trailing-log guard; the default would have left even more of the log in place.
The single node has no peers, so no vote, election or quorum consequence was measured.

review_items.rationale: The antecedent is declared before the result is read: the harness reports the receiver's own last entry and raw log index before the install and states that entries above the installed index are held, and the monitor only evaluates when the install was accepted. Nothing was filtered by the observed predicate, and no applicability condition depends on within_installed_snapshot. The recorded condition concerns whether removal by a later AppendEntries is an acceptable substitute for aligning at install time; that is a reading of the same protocol requirement, not a precondition for whether the requirement applies to this receiver.
limitations: The carrier is one node with one snapshot and one seeded log; other configurations of the installed index versus the tail are not covered.
Reachability under a live leader and the duration of the retained tail remain open.

resolutions.rationale: This condition states the very discrepancy the claim is about, so it is answered by fixing which duty the check encodes rather than by weakening it: the snapshot protocol requires a receiver that cannot confirm the snapshot's last included entry to discard the log, while the implementation removes such a tail only later, in appendEntries. S57 and S58 show the install-time handler adopting the snapshot's index and compacting no further than that index, S54 shows the surviving tail is what the node reports, and S8 shows the only later truncation. The completed execution 3d53c8e244184b0490a87411aabe15f4 demonstrates the state exists (two entries retained, lastApplied 3, effective last entry (5, 1)). The claim therefore asserts the install-time alignment duty, and the question of whether a later AppendEntries always arrives soon enough is retained as an outer boundary of applicability instead of being folded into the claim.

condition_dispositions.rationale: Whether the tail is always transient in a deployment is a separate question from whether the receiver owes alignment at install time. The claim's scope is the install-time duty, its harness alternative already records the transient reading, and this review carries the same boundary in its limitations.

scope_limitations: Whether relying on the next AppendEntries to truncate the tail is acceptable in every deployment remains open outside this claim.

resolutions.rationale: This is the harness-level record of the same protocol conflict, so it is answered with the same attributed reading. The harness introduces no weakening: it seeds the log in the caller-owned store, installs a snapshot through the production handler, and reports the handler's own bookkeeping without touching alignment logic, with the FSM restore and TrailingLogs adaptations declared in the plan. The conflict does not change any harness input, prerequisite, oracle or identity, so it is preserved as a boundary of the check rather than renamed into the driver.

condition_dispositions.rationale: The condition concerns when the tail is removed in a live deployment, while the harness legality rests on the seeded log, the accepted install and the reported bookkeeping. It is retained in the review limitations instead of being renamed into the driver.

scope_limitations: The check establishes the install-time state for one seeded carrier; it does not settle the deployment-level timing of the later truncation.
